own_solution.law: T = exp(-2aκ), κ = sqrt(2(mc²)(V-E))/(ħc), so a = (ħc)ln(1/T)/(2sqrt(2(mc²)(V-E))). Using mc² = 511000 eV and V-E = 3 eV gives κ = 8.87481 nm⁻¹.
assumptions: Use the stipulated exponential transmission model for the barrier approached by the electron.
The supplied electron mass and kinetic energy apply after any barrier replacement.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TFB05 and T6F0D omit the numerical height and unit, stating only 'a new value', whereas the other height variants specify 7.2 eV, violating the required preservation of number and unit.

notes: The base problem and every individual rendering have determinate answers under the supplied model; invalidity concerns the required variant construction. Changing the second barrier or a barrier used for an earlier run only does not change the target barrier's parameters. Both TDA04 and T8282 replace the target barrier before the relevant electron encounter, giving V-E = 2.2 eV and a = 0.454462 nm. Replacement explicitly describes a change over time, so the new height does not contradict the original height.
